jurisdictions.name: Carmel
jurisdictions.office: Building and Code Services, Community Services Department
jurisdictions.portal_name: Online Permitting, with plan upload through Project Dox
notes: Carmel applicants file a residential permit online, then get an email to upload plans to the Project Dox submittal system once a permit number is assigned.
The city says residential projects must meet the 2020 Indiana Residential Code, which is the 2018 IRC with the 2020 Indiana amendments.
Carmel's pool inspection procedures list bonding and grounding and final inspections, with the equipotential bonding grid checked against NEC Section 680.26.
For pools without a cover, the same document requires a fence at least 5 feet high with self-closing, self-latching, lockable gates, under a separate fence permit.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Inspection Procedures - City of Carmel Building and Code Services

jurisdictions.name: Westfield
notes: Westfield lists a Residential Pool (RP) permit for in-ground pools, submitted through its Citizens Portal after registering an account.
Required documents include a site or plot plan showing property lines, existing structures, right-of-way and all easements, with scale, north arrow and address or lot number.
The pool page lists a State Construction Design Release (CDR) and an Erosion Control Application among the documents to prepare.
Construction documents must include a pool plan and a cross-section drawing of the pool, and review does not guarantee full compliance with the Indiana Building Code.

sources.title: Apply for a Permit - City of Westfield

gaps: Only 2 jurisdictions verified. Indianapolis (indy.gov pages load only a script shell), Fort Wayne (Cloudflare/403), Fishers (Cloudflare), Evansville (403) and Bloomington (Cloudflare) could not be read.
Lafayette's residential projects page was opened but does not mention pools, so it was not used.
Carmel and Westfield: the code edition for pool barriers was not stated on the opened pages beyond the 2020 Indiana Residential Code (Carmel); Westfield does not name an edition.

Carmel's inspection document says the 5 ft fence rule, which is stricter than the state R326 4 ft figure on the existing JEBN page; the source was a city inspection procedure, so check with the city before relying on it.
